continuity_scope: Joe Abercrombie, The Blade Itself (Gollancz, 2006), original UK novel witness, restricted further to its opening six chapters: “The End,” “Questions,” “The Fencing Contest,” “No Choice at All,” “Teeth and Fingers,” and “The Wide and Barren North.” This is not a composite account of the First Law trilogy, standalones, Sharp Ends, Age of Madness, translations, revised/reformatted editions, audiobooks, or adaptations.

work_or_witnesses.edition: Gollancz, 2006, original UK novel edition (ISBN 9780575077850); 422 pages. Chapter, rather than page, locators are used because subsequent editions differ in pagination.
Official Joe Abercrombie sample PDF containing the declared opening chapter set; direct primary-text access witness.
Author's official book page, used for 2006 publication, Book One status, official synopsis, and authorized extract access.

coverage_rule: Include the three opening viewpoint protagonists (Logen Ninefingers, Sand dan Glokta, and Jezal dan Luthar) and their named continuing on-page companions or direct training authority in the first six chapters: Malacus Quai, Practical Severard, Practical Frost, and Lord Marshal Varuz. This seven-person cohort covers the early northern journey, the Inquisition interrogation team, and the fencing-training thread. Named one-scene prisoners, offstage/only-mentioned figures, groups, and everyone introduced after the declared chapter set remain outside scope. Peoples, military/social roles, institutions, magic, spirits, artifacts, places, and narrative archetypes remain dimensions/source terms.
omissions: All chapters after “The Wide and Barren North” in The Blade Itself, including later introductions, journeys, relationships, and the novel's resolution
Before They Are Hanged, Last Argument of Kings, all standalones, Sharp Ends, Age of Madness, other First Law-world works, every translation/reformatting/audiobook, and adaptations
Named one-scene detainees, offstage figures, collective military or institutional figures, and unnamed opponents in the declared opening chapters
Northmen, Shanka/Flatheads, Union subjects, the Inquisition, Practicals, the Magi, spirits, weapons, libraries, cities, and other non-individual concepts
uncertainties: The 2006 original and later print/ebook/audiobook editions have differing pagination and may have different paratext or translation titles. This pass cites exact chapter titles in the original English novel instead of applying a page number from a later edition.

The opening is delivered through limited, strongly subjective viewpoints. Glokta's judgments, Jezal's self-appraisal, and Logen's recollections are not treated as neutral omniscient evidence; records distinguish directly narrated actions from character framing where relevant.

Aliases, reputations, and past violence are intentionally limited to what the opening six chapters establish. Later explanation of Logen's identity, the Magi, the political plot, and every subsequent status change is excluded.

The declared chapters contain graphic violence, torture, coercive interrogation, war injury, threats, and stigmatizing language about disability/body difference. These are recorded descriptively and without endorsement or conversion into archetype labels. Fictional people and national groups are not mapped to real ones.
evidence_basis: Character, relationship, and term claims use Joe Abercrombie's authorized sample text, cited by exact original chapter title. The official author page provides the book's 2006/Book One context and an authorized extract; Google Books supplies bibliographic confirmation of the original Gollancz edition. No fan wiki or Wikipedia is used.
